research_rationale:
Whole-lifecycle YES claim for EO 12448 (Exercise of Authority Under Section 218 of Title 18, United States Code, November 4, 1983, 48 FR 51281), read in full from the held Federal Register text. Section 1 delegates to the head of each executive department, military department and executive agency the President's authority under 18 U.S.C. 218 to declare void and rescind transactions after a final conviction for a violation of chapter 11 of title 18. Section 2 lets those heads exercise the authority by regulation and requires the Secretary of Defense, the Administrator of General Services and the Administrator of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration jointly to issue government-wide implementing regulations on voiding or rescinding contracts. Section 3 and its paragraphs (a) to (d) fix the minimum procedural protections every implementing regulation must give (written notice, an opportunity to submit information, a hearing on request, and a written final decision stating restitution). The order has no date, expiry or condition and no revocation or supersession of another order. No later instrument amending or ending it is held: the packet chain has no events and the later-events OFR catalog search recorded 0 disposition notes. The current eCFR text of 48 CFR 3.703, held as a lead from the eCFR search as of 2026-10-14, still describes the order as the delegation of the President's authority under 18 U.S.C. 218, and the U.S. Code prints the order as a note to 18 U.S.C. 218 without an ending statement. The U.S. Code edition is current through 2026-10-09; that limit is stated, not filled.
